headline: turns/cost per rename — the rename study's primary metric (cost divided by rename-edits); jigc should be CHEAPER (one `jigc rename` command) where plain/static burn turns hand-editing and chasing referrers.
note: Rename-heavy by construction: all 8 edits are renames, so the per-rename cost denominator is well-powered (the small-N confound). Each non-compounding rename breaks >=1 NON-control forward edge: an `arch-doc cites` dangle is 2 hops (the far case a static rule is least likely to make a cold agent catch); a `supersedes` dangle is 1 hop. Edits 7-8 are compounding re-touches of docs renamed at edits 2-3 (they re-dangle only in an arm that REPAIRED the edit-2/3 dangle, e.g. the jigc arm under `jigc rename`). The `breaks` field is the edge(s) that newly dangle on a NON-repairing arm; the oracle (measure-refint.py) measures the actual HEAD per arm. Edit 4 is the DELIBERATELY NON-GREPPABLE referrer: its prompt is a semantic ticket that withholds the target slug `sticky-lb-affinity` (check-seed.sh fails if the slug leaks into prompts/edit-4.txt), so a plain/static agent that never derived the slug cannot grep its arch-doc referrer, while `jigc rename` resolves the slug + walks the edge index and repoints it. A transitive supersedes chain is greppable and is NOT this construction (ideas/cli-owned-rename.md -> Acceptance).
